subject: Re: Pricing follow-up - token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosts
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Menon <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up + quick benchmarking (post-call recap)

Hi Alex / Priya -

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking us through Acme's MAAP ingestion and downstream use cases. Quick recap + the asks you mentioned on the call so we can align on next steps: 

- Current expected steady-state volume: 6M tokens/day (burst to 10M/day) across extraction + enrichment pipelines.
- Primary model types: high-quality summarization and instruction-following (latency-sensitive, 1-3s p99 target), some embeddings for search.
- Security: data residency US, SOC2 required, will evaluate Private deployment for regulated tenants.
- Procurement / budget: you asked for target $/1M tokens benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and other hosted open-models, and a ballpark Redwood price and discounting for committed volumes.

Attached is a short benchmarking PDF (Redwood-pricing-vs-hosts-2026.pdf) - included rough apples-to-apples $/1M token comparisons and unit economics for baseline configs. Also attached is the usage workbook you shared filled with our quick calculations (Acme-MAAP-usage-estimates.xlsx).

High-level from our side (ballpark, non-binding):
- OpenAI equivalent (closed models): ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens for the highest-end model families you compared (low-latency, instruction tuned).
- Anthropic (comparable safety/tuning): ~ $400 / 1M tokens.
- Shared/open-model hosts (spot/shared infra for quantized LLMs): $200-250 / 1M tokens depending on latency and quantization.
- Redwood target for Acme with a committed-reserved plan (Dedicated capacity + 12M tokens/day equivalent commit): $250-350 / 1M tokens depending on model family, latency SLO, and KV/prefix caching opportunities.

Unit economics notes (very high-level):
- Estimated raw infra cost per 1M tokens (GPU + infra + networking): ~$70-120 depending on model and quantization.
- Redwood target margin and overlay (ops, SLA, observability): we typically price to land a 30-50% gross margin at scale.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm the 6M tokens/day steady-state (or correct the workbook) and expected read/write split?
2) Confirm if you need Private/VPC or Dedicated vs Hosted - that materially affects pricing and procurement timeline.
3) If the ballpark range looks reasonable, we can draft a committed pricing term sheet (12 month) and model a pilot for 30 days to validate latency and token delta.

Happy to hop on another 30-min call this week to walk the workbook line-by-line.

Thanks -
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-vs-hosts-2026.pdf (summary benchmarking), Acme-MAAP-usage-estimates.xlsx (populated)

From: Alex Johnson <alex@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up + quick benchmarking (post-call recap)

Thanks Vanessa - really helpful, appreciate the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from our end: 

- The 6M tokens/day is our conservative estimate for production; proof-of-concept will likely be ~1.5M/day. We expect ramp to 6M/day within 3 months of rollout.
- Read/write split: ~70% generation (outputs), 30% input tokens.
- Primary ask from procurement: target $/1M tokens goal of <= $300 if we commit to a 12-month reserved plan and agree on an SLA. We also need clarity on how prefix/KV caching will be handled since that will reduce net token counts for us.

Can you confirm whether the $250-350 / 1M figure you quoted for Redwood is achievable at 12M/day committed or whether that was for 12M tokens/month? Also, please call out any onboarding credits or pilot terms you can offer.

If you can send a 1-pager with committed pricing tiers (pilot, committed monthly, enterprise reserved), we can share with procurement and return with our budgets.

-fAlex
Alex Johnson
Head of Data Products | Acme Analytics
alex@acme-analytics.com | (206) 555-0108

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing follow-up + quick benchmarking (Acme) - procurement asked for <= $300/1M with 12m reserved

Marissa / Aditya -

Looping you in on Acme's reply. Key asks: they want <= $300 / 1M tokens with a 12-month reserved plan (they estimate steady-state 6M/day after ramp). They also asked for clarity on whether our $250-350 band was per-month or per-day commit - I mistakenly left that ambiguous in the initial note (my bad). To confirm: our earlier band was per 1M tokens with the expectation of a 12-month committed capacity (they are not asking for 12M/day commit - they want pricing tied to tokens consumed with a 12-month contract and a ~12M tokens/month commit floor to get aggressive pricing).

Quick ask: can you run margin/pricing calc for a modeled commit of 12M tokens/month (which is ~400k tokens/day) vs their stated production need (6M/day) - but for quoting we should focus on the committed floor they can contract to for procurement (12M/month). They are targeting $300 / 1M - is that doable for our standard Dedicated offering (or would it require Reserved/Private and additional discounting)?

Points to validate: 
- What level of prefix/KV caching do we expect for their workload (assume 20-30% token savings baseline).
- Model family assumptions (we should propose an open-model quantized instance vs our highest-latency-tuned pod). If we need to offer lowest-latency closed-model variant, price will be higher.
- Pilot terms: we usually provide 1-2 weeks of free pilot credits for latency validation; for a committed deal we can front-load credits against the first invoice.

If you send me a 1-pager and a quick tiered pricing table I can return to Alex with a clean committed offer.

Thanks -
Vanessa

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Menon <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed committed pricing tiers + next steps (Acme)

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks for the clarification - and for the target of <= $300 / 1M tokens. Based on your ask and the usage workbook, here is a clean, non-binding committed pricing proposal to share with procurement quickly: 

Proposed committed tiers (12-month term):
- Pilot (30 days, non-committed): Host evaluation on Redwood shared-hosted cluster; up to 1.5M tokens/day; credits: $10k applied to first invoice. Price: pay-as-you-go equivalent $400 / 1M tokens.
- Committed Standard (12M tokens/month commit): $320 / 1M tokens. Includes 20% discount off list, standard SLA (99.9%), prefix/KV caching enabled (we estimate 20-30% effective token savings).
- Committed Reserved (24M tokens/month commit OR Dedicated capacity with 6-month notice): $290 / 1M tokens. Includes priority capacity, 99.95% SLA, and 30% caching estimate.
- Enterprise Private (VPC / on-prem managed): pricing by quote (typically $250-280 / 1M tokens at scale after infra pass-through).

Notes / unit economics:
- The $320 / 1M for the 12M/month commit is achievable on our standard Dedicated configs; $290 requires either a larger commit or moving to Dedicated Reserved pools with some operational commitments.

- We model GPU-level infra cost at ~$90 / 1M tokens for the model family we tested; with caching the net $/effective 1M tokens improves materially.

- These numbers assume their workload fits the quantized open-model profile; closed-model (highest-latency, proprietary variants) will be higher and closer to the OpenAI-equivalent band.

Recommended next steps:
1) We share this 1-pager with Acme procurement. If they confirm which tier they prefer, we will prepare a simple MSA + SOW with the committed term and a pilot addendum.
2) Tech validation: schedule 1-week pilot (we can provision test endpoints) and run their 1.5M/day PoC to validate latency and caching benefits.
3) Procurement: for committed tiers we will outline billing cadence and the credit/backstop terms (we typically apply pilot credits to first invoice).

If this looks good I can put together a short PDF 1-pager and a draft term sheet (DocuSign link) for signatures.

Suggested ask from you: which committed tier should I draft (Committed Standard at $320/1M or Committed Reserved at $290/1M)?

Thanks - look forward to closing this quickly.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-vs-hosts-2026.pdf, Acme-MAAP-usage-estimates.xlsx
